correctness.rationale: The classical sixty points and sixty planes give separate vertex sets and the stated algebraic bilinear zero test. I reconstructed the projectively normalized supports in F_37 with i mapped to 6: each Gaussian dot product is a+bi with |a|,|b|≤4, so a+6b has magnitude at most 28 and vanishes mod 37 exactly when a=b=0. The integer incidence matrix has degree 15 on both sides and 900 edges. Exact characteristic polynomials agree, including simplicity of the zero Laplacian root; the cofactor determinant is 2^235·3^15·5^48·7^30. Direct integer Smith reduction of the 119-by-119 cofactor returned 64 ones and factors 2^×7, 4, 20^×3, 40^×14, 1120^×16, 4480^×3, 13440^×7, 40320^×3, 201600, where × denotes multiplicity. The product and divisibility check, so all primes and multiplicities are accounted for. The frozen verifier's local proof also uses valid equivalences: unit pivots split factors, and reducing precision on division by p of the entire residual block preserves the remaining information. No pivot reaches the cutoff.
residual_risks: The block-matrix display around RESULT.md line 42 has a missing row-separator backslash; the intended block Laplacian is unambiguous from the incidence definition, degree and code.
Verifies the characteristic-zero model; no analogous positive-characteristic configuration or canonical geometric degeneration is established.

value.rationale: This is the complete integer chip-firing invariant of a standard 120-vertex geometric Levi graph. In particular it gives a minimal generator count of 55, exponent 201600, and the precise local structure beyond the tree number. Those data are useful for computations with divisors on this graph and for the component group of a regular split unit-thickness model with this dual graph; the graph is motivated independently of its answer and the invariant is not a repackaging of the spectrum.
residual_risks: A finite exact invariant, not a classification for other Klein graphs or a proof of canonical geometric realization in a smoothing of the original arrangement.
